newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dlr ends down as military buys greenback.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dlr ends down as military buys greenback.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed sharply lower against its U.S. counterpart on Monday, reflecting foreign fund outflows and strong military demand for the American currency to pay for scheduled arms imports, dealers said.
The local unit closed at T$27.909 against Saturday's T$27.859 finish.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$292.5 million.
Dealers said the military apparently bought U.S. dollars to meet routine arms payments.
"There was strong military buying of the U.S. dollar, despite the U.S. dollar's weakness overseas," said one dealer.
"But it was a one-session thing and the Taiwan dollar is not expected to fall fast," she said.
But other dealers said an outflow of foreign funds may intensify if investors begin to take profits against the Taiwan stock market's recent sharp gains as they did in March and April.
A T$27.88-91 range was seen for Tuesday.
